title: NVIDIA locks in 2GW of Australian AI-factory capacity across eight partners by 2027
subtitle: Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, Megaport, ResetData, CDC, NEXTDC, and AirTrunk will host multiple generations of NVIDIA DSX compute — IREN's Bundey campus alone targets 800MW.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: NVIDIA announced on September 9, 2026 that it will expand AI-compute capacity in Australia to up to 2 gigawatts by 2027, working with eight domestic cloud and data-center operators: Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, Megaport, ResetData, CDC, NEXTDC, and AirTrunk. The deal covers land, power, and shell capacity for multiple generations of the NVIDIA DSX AI-factory architecture — the same reference design NVIDIA has been rolling out in the US, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. IREN's planned Bundey campus in South Australia alone is designed for 800MW of eventual capacity; Firmus is expanding its Project Southgate initiative to host hyperscale demand across Australia and Asia-Pacific.

The reason this matters is the emerging geography of frontier compute. Until this year, the AI-factory buildout has concentrated in three regions: the US Gulf and Mountain West, the Gulf states, and northern Europe. Australia's addition — 2GW is roughly the total AI-training capacity Meta had online in mid-2025 — puts a fourth region on the map, with grid characteristics different from all three. Australia has abundant land, direct fiber to Singapore and Los Angeles, and an energy mix that is aggressively transitioning to solar and battery storage. NVIDIA is buying into that mix, and it is buying it early enough that the physical shells are being designed around DSX rather than retrofitted.

This is also the second sovereign-scale AI-factory commitment in eight days. On September 1, we covered EuroHPC's LUMI-AI decision for the Kajaani site — €387M and an AMD MI430X-based cluster. The Australia announcement is bigger by roughly an order of magnitude in raw capacity, and it is coming through commercial data-center operators rather than a research consortium. Read together, the two decisions say that the compute-buildout window through 2027 is now fully overlapping with the sovereign-AI window: countries and hyperscalers are placing their bets on the same 18-month horizon.

Takeaway for learners: if you want to work on frontier AI systems, geography is starting to matter again. The last decade of ML careers happened in Silicon Valley and London because that is where the H100s were. The next decade will happen in more places — Australia, Finland, Saudi Arabia, Texas, Ohio — because that is where the DSX and MI430X factories are getting built. Look at where the shells are going up, and follow the physical infrastructure. That is where the jobs will be, and where the interesting work will land.
